INTEGRATION_CONTRACT_V1CP section 3 already says the clinical hold's only exit is a readiness declaration, and that restartProgram reads standing holds from the record, never only from referenceState.
cfObs1.Q1_sourceOfTruth: The record: a readable CLINICAL_HOLD row of this athlete (sealed, intact, string id, not foreign or orphan, dated at or before the decision clock), held under server custody. referenceState is a derived continuation cache: it may add restriction (sticky clinical pending) but can never establish that no hold stands. On disagreement the more restrictive reading wins.
cfObs1.Q2_standingHold: One predicate, shared by evaluateProgram, withHoldFact, restartIntake and the server: the hold is standing when such a row exists and no later readable READINESS_DECLARED of this athlete that validly answers it (all signs no, declaredRecovered, eligibility after the hold, named hold matching when named) follows it. Any unreadable F08 row means HOLD (SB-3), never 'no hold'. Computed from the record on every call, whatever reference is sent.

Q3_absentInvalidStale.invalid (digest, ownership, future clock: HOLD as today, no plan; the server never forwards it (and the client gets 'send the stored state').
Q3_absentInvalidStale.absent or stale (valid but older than th: read the hold from the record. If it stands: READINESS_DECLARATION is evaluated by its handler (the release path); RETURN_AFTER_PAUSE and NOT_FEELING_100 / WELLBEING_CHECK facts are screened (clinical first, D5 guidance) and recorded append-only but never release and prescribe nothing; every other kind (WEEKLY_REVIEW, MISSED_SESSION, SYSTEMIC_FATIGUE, SCHEDULE_CHANGE, GOAL_CHANGE, EVENT_DATE_CHANGE, ...) returns CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED with no proposal. If no hold stands, proceed; whether a non-clinical pending question lost with a stale reference must be re-asked is QRE's (Security only requires that it never lowers a clinical hold).
Q3_absentInvalidStale.restartProgram: already reads the record; keep it.

cfObs1.Q4_release: A legitimate resumption is preserved because the release is itself a recorded fact: after a valid READINESS_DECLARED the predicate of Q2 reads the hold as released, with or without the reference, so the next review plans normally. Nothing else releases a hold unless the competent authority defines another explicit release fact (for example a qualified clearance by a professional, if PCG/SSCTR and the Founder ever want one): recorded, attributable to an authenticated actor, server-timestamped, naming the hold, in the inventory. 'The next review sent without the reference state' is never an admissible representation of a release or a clearance: absence of state is indistinguishable from data loss, a new or restored device, a client bug, a rollback, an attacker or the athlete bypassing the hold, and the reference digest is keyless so even a 'clean' reference proves nothing (p11). The 28 qualified-clearance tests encode that representation; when CF-OBS-1 is fixed they must be migrated to an explicit release fact (their owners decide how; R7-D stays closed and is not reopened by this record).

server: Custody: the server stores the authoritative append-only record and the latest reference state per athlete and program; ids and timestamps are server-assigned; the review input is composed from the stored copies (or the client's copies are accepted only when their hashes equal the stored heads).
Concurrency: a review against a record head, program hash or reference that is not the latest stored is refused (no evaluation), so a stale device cannot plan over a later hold.
Append-only on store: a returned record must extend the stored one (prefix equality); an absent actualLedger means unchanged (OBS-FFC-01).

Defence in depth until the core rule exists: the server evaluates the Q2 predicate itself and delivers no prescription (plan sync, notifications, calendar, watch or Health export) while a hold stands, whatever the engine returned.
Release only through the readiness-declaration endpoint (or a future explicit release fact), authenticated as the athlete, audited.
No health-derived field in logs, analytics, crash reports or OS surfaces (C4, C5).
client: Never builds, edits, re-seals or drops referenceState or the record; sends exactly what the server holds.
Shows the decision's guidance immediately; shows no prescription while the status is CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED; on HOLD shows nothing new.
Offline evaluation, if any, is provisional and never shows prescriptions while the stored record holds a standing hold.

Q6_testing: A negative matrix: every review kind x reference {current, absent, stale pre-hold, invalid digest, foreign athlete, future clock, client-re-sealed clean} x record {standing hold, released by a valid declaration, hold row altered, unsealed, deleted, record absent, record not an array}. Oracle: while a hold stands, no decision carries a proposal with live prescriptions (CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED or HOLD only), signs still set the guidance, the record stays append-only and sealed.

A monotonicity property (fuzz, QRE harness): replacing the current reference by absent, stale or re-sealed never yields a less restrictive outcome while the record holds a standing hold; mutation tests must kill a mutant that drops the record check.

Release parity: a valid readiness declaration releases with and without the reference, and the next review plans; invalid declarations (a sign yes, a screen before the hold, a wrong named hold) never release.
A test that dropping the reference never releases, replacing the 'qualified clearance by ref:null' model in the migrated tests.
Integration-level tests: the server refuses stale heads, absent or re-sealed references, non-prefix records; no prescription leaves the server during a hold. Synthetic data and canaries only.
